post.summary:
Clear deletes exactly the records captured by the Export/Transfer run that produced the
manifest. Memories recalled (or re-created) since the capture survive, as do events that
still have memories.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Clear deletes exactly the records captured by the Export/Transfer run that produced the
manifest: memories are deleted only if neither created nor recalled since the snapshot, and
events only once they have no memories left. Manifests are held in memory - a restart discards
them.

post.summary:
ExplainConsolidation reports where individual memories stand against the consolidation rules -
each one's computed value, the threshold it is measured against, and how long it has before it
crosses - together with the capacity pressure scaling that threshold and, optionally, the decay
curve the configured algorithm produces. It reads nothing but the memories named in the
request and deletes nothing.
post.description:
Where PreviewConsolidation answers "what would a cycle forget now" across the whole store,
this answers "where does this memory stand, and when is it due" for memories the caller
already has in hand - which is why it needs only the reader tier: it enumerates nothing.
Rejected with FailedPrecondition on a read/write replica (consolidation.enabled: false),
whose configuration is not the one its store is consolidated under.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
ExplainConsolidationRequest asks where the named memories stand against the consolidation rules,
and optionally for the decay curve of the current configuration. Both parts are optional: ids
without a curve values just those memories, a curve without ids reports the configuration and the
current capacity pressure alone. Ids that do not exist are simply absent from the response.

get.summary:
GetEvents lists events filtered by time range, significance range, group, and metadata,
paginated by limit/offset (see GetEventsRequest). significance_extremum swaps the
significance_min/max range for "only events tied at the highest (or lowest) significance
value" instead. order_by/order_dir choose the sort field and direction.

parameters.name: timeStartMin
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive lower bound on time_start; 0 (the default) means no lower bound

parameters.name: timeStartMax
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive upper bound on time_start; 0 (the default) means no upper bound

parameters.name: timeEndMin
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive lower bound on time_end; 0 (the default) means no lower bound

parameters.name: timeEndMax
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive upper bound on time_end; 0 (the default) means no upper bound

parameters.name: significanceMin
parameters.description: inclusive lower bound on significance; 0 (the default) means no bound, NOT a literal significance-of-zero filter

parameters.name: significanceMax
parameters.description: inclusive upper bound on significance; 0 (the default) means no bound, NOT a literal significance-of-zero filter

parameters.name: memories
parameters.description: when true, include each matching event's memories in the response

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: optional: restrict to events carrying this group label

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: the field to sort on; defaults to "significance". One of: "significance" (naturally desc, then time_start, then id), "timestamp" (time_start, naturally desc), "time_end" (naturally desc; an event that has not ended stores 0, so those sort as the OLDEST rather than the most recent - use time_end_min to exclude them), "name" (naturally asc), "group" (naturally asc, then time_start), "link_significance" (naturally desc, then significance), "id" (naturally asc). order_dir overrides the natural direction. Every ordering carries an id tiebreaker, so offset pagination is stable

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: page size; a value <= 0 selects the server default (25); values above the server cap (200) are silently clamped down to it

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: rows to skip for pagination; negative values are clamped to 0; no upper bound

parameters.name: significanceExtremum
parameters.description:
when set, ignore significance_min/significance_max and return only events tied at that significance value among the other filters (time range, group, metadata) - not a range; 0 (default) applies no extremum

 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_UNSPECIFIED: no extremum filtering; significance_min/significance_max (if set) apply as a normal range
 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_HIGHEST: return only events at the highest significance value among those matching the other filters
 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_LOWEST: return only events at the lowest significance value among those matching the other filters

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: optional: restrict to events whose metadata carries every one of these "key=value" pairs (AND, exact match), exactly as GetMemoriesRequest.metadata

parameters.name: memoryCounts
parameters.description: when true, populate each returned event's memory_count. Separate from `memories` and opt-in because it is a second query per page: it reports how many memories an event holds without transferring any of them, which is what a listing wants and what `memories` is far too expensive for

parameters.name: orderDir
parameters.description:
optional: reverse order_by's sort direction; UNSPECIFIED (the default) uses that field's natural direction. Applies to the whole ordering, tiebreakers included, so ASC returns exactly the reverse of DESC

 - SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: sort in the order_by field's natural direction (see above)
 - SORT_DIRECTION_ASC: ascending, whatever the field's natural direction
 - SORT_DIRECTION_DESC: descending, whatever the field's natural direction

post.summary:
Events
StoreEvent creates an event, optionally with nested memories (each defaulted to the new
event's id when unset). An event below event.minimumSignificance is quietly dropped - see
StoreEventResponse.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Event is a named time span with its own significance, optionally carrying links to
other events and/or nested memories. memories/links are populated on read only when
requested (GetEventById, GetEvents); on StoreEvent nested memories are write-only input, each
stored via the same rules as StoreMemory.

post.summary:
MergeEvents re-points every memory of merge_from onto merge_to. merge_to must already exist;
merge_from need not - an absent one simply matches no memories.

SummariseMemories condenses an event's memories into a single summary using the optional
embedded LLM (ollama.enabled), then replaces them with it exactly as ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary
does - so the service generates the summary the caller would otherwise have to supply. Fails
with FAILED_PRECONDITION when no summariser is configured. See SummariseMemoriesRequest.

Summarisation
ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary deletes every memory of an event and replaces them with a single
caller-supplied summary memory, in one transaction; see ReplaceMemoriesWithSummaryRequest.

get.summary:
GetEventById fetches a single event by id; set memories to also load its nested memories.
NotFound if the event does not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the event to fetch

parameters.name: memories
parameters.description: true also loads the event's memories into the response

parameters.name: memoryCounts
parameters.description: true populates memory_count, exactly as GetEventsRequest.memory_counts does (and for the same reason: it reports how many memories the event holds without transferring any of them)

delete.summary:
DeleteEvent deletes an event. When memories is true its memories are deleted too; otherwise
they are kept but detached (their event_id is cleared). NotFound if the event does not exist.

parameters.name: memories
parameters.description: true also deletes the event's memories; false only detaches them

post.summary:
EndEvent sets an event's time_end (defaults to now when unset). NotFound if the event does
not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the event to end

get.summary: GetEventLinks is GetMemoryLinks for events; the same rules apply.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the event whose links to return; must exist

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description:
which directions to return; unset means BOTH

 - LINK_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: treated as BOTH
 - LINK_DIRECTION_BOTH: links in either direction
 - LINK_DIRECTION_OUTBOUND: only links this item declared, pointing away from it
 - LINK_DIRECTION_INBOUND: only links other items declared, pointing at it

post.summary: LinkEvents is LinkMemories for events; the same rules apply.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the event the links start from; must exist

post.summary: UnlinkEvents is UnlinkMemories for events; the same rules apply.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the event the links start from; must exist

patch.summary:
UpdateEventSignificance changes an event's significance, either as an absolute value or via
placement (see SignificancePlacement). NotFound if the event does not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the event to update

post.summary:
Transfer and archive (embedded -> centralised)
Export snapshots the whole store into an archive object in S3 and records a manifest of
exactly what was captured; with clear set, the captured records are deleted once the upload
has succeeded.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Export snapshots every event and memory into an archive object in S3 and records a manifest of
exactly what was captured; with clear set, the captured records are deleted after a successful
upload (writes and recalls landing mid-run survive, exactly as Clear does).

post.summary:
Import streams an archive object from S3 into the store, upserting every record by id with
its full state preserved. Idempotent; aborts on the first error.

ImportBatch upserts full-state rows by id directly - the ingest half of Transfer. Nothing is
defaulted or gated on minimum significance; the rows carry their history.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
ImportBatchRequest carries full-state rows (original timestamps, recall state, significance,
group, event links) to be upserted by id into the store as-is - a data migration, not a fresh
write. It is the ingest half of Transfer and is re-sendable: re-importing the same rows is
idempotent.

get.summary:
GetMemories lists memories filtered by time range, significance range, group, metadata, and
recall state (recalled/recall_count/time_recalled, plus is_summary and is_binary), paginated
by limit/offset (see GetMemoriesRequest). significance_extremum swaps the significance_min/max
range for "only memories tied at the highest (or lowest) significance value" instead.
order_by/order_dir choose the sort field and direction.

parameters.name: timestampMin
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive lower bound on time_stamp; 0 (the default) means no lower bound

parameters.name: timestampMax
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive upper bound on time_stamp; 0 (the default) means no upper bound

parameters.name: significanceMin
parameters.description: inclusive lower bound on significance; 0 (the default) means no bound, NOT a literal significance-of-zero filter

parameters.name: significanceMax
parameters.description: inclusive upper bound on significance; 0 (the default) means no bound, NOT a literal significance-of-zero filter

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: optional: restrict to memories carrying this group label

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: the field to sort on; defaults to "significance". One of: "significance" (naturally desc, then time_stamp, then id), "timestamp" (time_stamp, naturally desc), "time_recalled" (naturally desc; a never-recalled memory stores 0, so those sort as the LEAST recently recalled rather than being excluded - use recalled to ask about them), "recall_count" (naturally desc, then time_stamp), "group" (naturally asc, then time_stamp), "link_significance" (naturally desc, then significance), "id" (naturally asc). order_dir overrides the natural direction. Every ordering carries an id tiebreaker, so offset pagination is stable

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: page size; a value <= 0 selects the server default (25); values above the server cap (200) are silently clamped down to it

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: rows to skip for pagination; negative values are clamped to 0; no upper bound

parameters.name: significanceExtremum
parameters.description:
when set, ignore significance_min/significance_max and return only memories tied at that significance value among the other filters (time range, group, metadata, recall state) - not a range; 0 (default) applies no extremum

 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_UNSPECIFIED: no extremum filtering; significance_min/significance_max (if set) apply as a normal range
 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_HIGHEST: return only events at the highest significance value among those matching the other filters
 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_LOWEST: return only events at the lowest significance value among those matching the other filters

parameters.name: linkedTo
parameters.description: optional: restrict to memories linked to this memory id, in either direction (one hop). NotFound if that memory does not exist

parameters.name: links
parameters.description: when true, populate each returned memory's links

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: optional: restrict to memories whose metadata carries every one of these "key=value" pairs (AND, exact match). Split on the FIRST '=', so a value may itself contain '='; the key must match the metadata key charset. A repeated string rather than a map because a map cannot be bound from a URL query string - over HTTP this is ?metadata=source%3Dslack&metadata=project%3Dx. Unindexed, exactly as the group filter is

parameters.name: recalled
parameters.description:
optional: FALSE returns only never-recalled memories (recall_count = 0), TRUE only those recalled at least once; UNSPECIFIED (default) applies no restriction. This is what answers "what have I never recalled?" - recall_count_max cannot, because 0 there means no bound

 - UNSPECIFIED: not set; on Memory.is_binary the server treats this the same as FALSE, on a filter it applies no restriction
 - FALSE: explicitly false
 - TRUE: explicitly true

parameters.name: recallCountMin
parameters.description: inclusive lower bound on recall_count; 0 (the default) means no bound, NOT a literal never-recalled filter - use recalled for that

parameters.name: recallCountMax
parameters.description: inclusive upper bound on recall_count; 0 (the default) means no bound, NOT a literal never-recalled filter - use recalled for that

parameters.name: timeRecalledMin
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive lower bound on time_recalled; 0 (the default) means no lower bound. Both bounds ask only about memories that HAVE been recalled - see time_recalled_max

parameters.name: timeRecalledMax
parameters.description: UnixNano inclusive upper bound on time_recalled; 0 (the default) means no upper bound. Never-recalled memories are excluded rather than matched: their time_recalled is 0, so "recalled before X" would otherwise return every memory that was never recalled at all. Use recalled to ask about those

parameters.name: isSummary
parameters.description:
optional: TRUE returns only summary memories (see ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary), FALSE only non-summaries; UNSPECIFIED (default) applies no restriction

 - UNSPECIFIED: not set; on Memory.is_binary the server treats this the same as FALSE, on a filter it applies no restriction
 - FALSE: explicitly false
 - TRUE: explicitly true

parameters.name: isBinary
parameters.description:
optional: TRUE returns only binary memories, FALSE only non-binary; UNSPECIFIED (default) applies no restriction

 - UNSPECIFIED: not set; on Memory.is_binary the server treats this the same as FALSE, on a filter it applies no restriction
 - FALSE: explicitly false
 - TRUE: explicitly true

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: optional: restrict to memories associated with this event. This is the paged way to read an event's memories - GetEventById with memories: true returns them all in one message, which overruns the receive frame on a large event. Empty (the default) applies no restriction rather than matching the event-less; use has_event for those

parameters.name: hasEvent
parameters.description:
optional: FALSE returns only memories associated with no event, TRUE only those associated with one; UNSPECIFIED (default) applies no restriction. Exists because event_id cannot say it - an event-less memory stores an empty event_id, which is the same value that means "no bound" there, exactly as recalled exists alongside recall_count_min/max

 - UNSPECIFIED: not set; on Memory.is_binary the server treats this the same as FALSE, on a filter it applies no restriction
 - FALSE: explicitly false
 - TRUE: explicitly true

parameters.name: orderDir
parameters.description:
optional: reverse order_by's sort direction; UNSPECIFIED (the default) uses that field's natural direction. Applies to the whole ordering, tiebreakers included, so ASC returns exactly the reverse of DESC

 - SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: sort in the order_by field's natural direction (see above)
 - SORT_DIRECTION_ASC: ascending, whatever the field's natural direction
 - SORT_DIRECTION_DESC: descending, whatever the field's natural direction

post.summary:
Memories
StoreMemory creates a memory. A memory below memory.minimumSignificance is quietly dropped -
see StoreMemoryResponse.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Memory is a blob, opaque to the server, with a significance and timestamp, optionally linked to
an event. Recalling it (RecallMemories) reinforces it: the decay clock resets and its effective
significance rises. is_binary controls whether the body is indexed for content search (see
SearchMemories) - a binary body is never indexed.

post.summary: DeleteMemories deletes the given memories by id; unknown ids are silently ignored.

get.summary:
GetForgottenMemories reads the forgotten log: one record per memory the sleep cycle actually
deleted, with the decision that took it. Where PreviewConsolidation answers "what would go"
and ExplainConsolidation "where does this memory stand", this answers "what went, and why" -
the only one of the three that can speak about a memory that no longer exists.
get.description:
It is optional and off by default (consolidation.tombstones.enabled): a store that is not
recording returns an empty log rather than an error, since "nothing was recorded" is the
honest answer to what was forgotten. Records carry no body - a tombstone reports that
something was lost and is deliberately not an undelete.

parameters.name: memoryId
parameters.description: a specific memory - "did this exist, and when did it go"

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description:
UNSPECIFIED returns both rules

 - FORGET_RULE_CONSOLIDATION: decayed value fell below the capacity-pressure-scaled deletion threshold
 - FORGET_RULE_EVICTION: still above the threshold, but evicted to bring the store back under its byte capacity

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: UnixNano, inclusive lower bound on forgotten_at

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: UnixNano, exclusive upper bound on forgotten_at

parameters.name: afterSeq
parameters.description: pagination: return records below this seq (pass the lowest seq of the previous page)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: <= 0 selects the default (100), values above the cap (1000) are clamped down to it

post.summary: DeleteForgottenMemories empties the forgotten log, or the part of it older than before_time.
post.description:
It exists because the log's automatic bounds (consolidation.tombstones.maxRows/maxAgeInDays)
only apply while recording is enabled: turning the feature off deliberately leaves what was
already recorded in place, so that a configuration change never destroys a record somebody
kept. Removing it is therefore always an explicit request - this one.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
DeleteForgottenMemoriesRequest empties the forgotten log. Supply before_time to delete only what
was forgotten before it, or all to empty the log entirely - one of the two is required, so an
empty request can never silently discard the whole log.

post.summary:
RecallMemories returns the requested memories and reinforces each one: its recall time is
reset to now (resetting its decay clock) and its recall count is incremented (raising its
effective significance during consolidation). A reader-tier caller for whom reinforcement is
disabled (auth.readerRecallReinforces) gets a plain, non-reinforcing read instead; writer and
admin callers always reinforce.

SearchMemories finds memories via the optional content-search index; see
SearchMemoriesRequest.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
SearchMemoriesRequest queries the secondary content-search index for memories matching the
query. Results are always re-read from the primary store, which remains authoritative; ids the
index returns that the primary store no longer holds are silently dropped. When reinforce is
true the matched memories are recalled - resetting their decay clocks and raising their
effective significance - rather than merely fetched, and only the memories actually returned are
reinforced.

patch.summary:
UpdateMemory applies a partial update to an existing memory: only the fields carrying a value
(significance, body, event_id, group, time_stamp) overwrite the stored row. is_binary and
is_summary are NOT updatable here - they are set at creation and by ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary
- so any updated content must stay consistent with the memory's existing is_binary/is_summary:
a non-binary memory is re-indexed for content search, so its new body must remain valid text,
and a summary memory should keep summary-appropriate content. An unknown id returns NotFound
(no memory is created).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: auto-generated UUID if omitted on create; max 128 characters

get.summary:
GetMemoryLinks returns a memory's links. By default both directions are returned (the graph is
stored directed but valued symmetrically); set direction to narrow it. NotFound if the memory
does not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the memory whose links to return; must exist

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description:
which directions to return; unset means BOTH

 - LINK_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: treated as BOTH
 - LINK_DIRECTION_BOTH: links in either direction
 - LINK_DIRECTION_OUTBOUND: only links this item declared, pointing away from it
 - LINK_DIRECTION_INBOUND: only links other items declared, pointing at it

post.summary:
LinkMemories adds or updates links from one memory to others. Re-linking an existing pair
overwrites that link's significance rather than adding a second link. NotFound if the memory
or any target does not exist; InvalidArgument on a self-link or once the memory would exceed
the per-item link limit.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the memory the links start from; must exist

post.summary:
UnlinkMemories removes links from one memory to the named memories; unknown targets are
silently ignored. NotFound if the memory itself does not exist.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: the memory the links start from; must exist

post.summary:
Purge deletes every event and memory in the store. While it runs, all other Hippocampus RPCs
are rejected with Unavailable.

Sleep manually triggers a consolidation cycle out of schedule and resets the periodic timer.
Rejected with FailedPrecondition on a read/write replica (consolidation.enabled: false),
which must never run its own cycle.

get.summary:
PreviewConsolidation reports what a consolidation cycle would forget if one ran now, and
deletes nothing. It is the dry run for Sleep: the same decision rules, applied to the same
store, with the outcome returned instead of applied. Rejected with FailedPrecondition on a
read/write replica (consolidation.enabled: false), which never runs a cycle of its own and so
has nothing to preview.
get.description:
It is a separate RPC rather than a flag on Sleep so that the two can be authorised
separately - previewing what would be forgotten is a read, triggering it is not.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: memories to detail; <= 0 selects the default (100), values above the cap (1000) are clamped down to it

get.summary:
GetSummarisationCandidates returns events identified by the most recent sleep cycle as having
accumulated enough quiet, unsummarised memories to be worth condensing via
ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary. A point-in-time snapshot, refreshed only when
consolidation.summarisationMinMemories is configured.

post.summary:
Transfer streams the whole store directly into a centralised instance's ImportBatch RPC,
recording a manifest like Export; with clear set the captured records are deleted once the
target has accepted every batch.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description:
Transfer streams every event and memory directly to a centralised instance's ImportBatch RPC
(address from transfer.targetAddress); like Export it records a manifest, and with clear set
deletes the captured records once the target has accepted them all.

get.summary:
WhoAmI reports the authenticated caller's identity and effective authorization tier
(reader/writer/admin), so a client - the web console - can tailor what it offers instead of
guessing at the token's roles. Requires only the reader tier. When the service runs without
authentication it reports auth_enabled false and an unrestricted (admin) tier.

timeEnd.title: UnixNano; 0 (the default) uses the current server time

links.title: the targets and their significances; each target must exist and must not be id itself
the targets and their significances; each target must exist and must not be id itself

HippocampusLinkMemoriesBody.description:
LinkMemoriesRequest adds or updates links from one memory to others. It is an upsert per pair:
re-linking an existing pair overwrites that link's significance rather than creating a duplicate.

significance.title: optional: significance for the resulting summary memory; 0 (and no placement) defaults to the highest significance among the replaced memories

placement.title: optional: rank the summary relative to existing values (see SignificancePlacement); takes precedence over significance when set

HippocampusSummariseMemoriesBody.description:
SummariseMemoriesRequest asks the service to generate a summary of an event's memories with the
embedded LLM (ollama.enabled) and replace them with it in one transaction, like
ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary but with the service authoring the summary. Binary memories are
excluded from the LLM prompt (their bodies are opaque, not text).

ids.title: targets to unlink; unknown ids are silently ignored. Removes links in either direction between id and each target
targets to unlink; unknown ids are silently ignored. Removes links in either direction between id and each target

significance.title: the new absolute significance; must be >= 1 to take effect. IMPORTANT: 0 with no placement is a no-op - it leaves the event's existing significance unchanged; there is no way to reset an event to unranked via this RPC

placement.title: write-only: rank relative to existing values (see SignificancePlacement); takes precedence over significance when set

timeStamp.title: UnixNano; defaults to the current time when unset (0) on create; required (> 0) once defaulted

significance.title: 0 = unranked (rank it later via UpdateMemory/placement); must be >= 0; higher ranks more significant. On UpdateMemory, 0 with no placement leaves the existing significance unchanged - it cannot reset a memory to unranked

eventId.title: optional: leave unset to store the memory unassociated with any event

body.title: required (non-empty) on create; a proto3 string, so always valid UTF-8 on the wire - encode true binary payloads (e.g. base64) before setting is_binary; optionally capped by memory.limit.sizeBytes (0 = unlimited)

isBinary.title: set once at creation; not updatable via UpdateMemory. TRUE bodies are opaque and never indexed for content search (see SearchMemories)

timeRecalled.title: read-only: UnixNano of the most recent recall (RecallMemories, or SearchMemories with reinforce); 0 if never recalled; ignored on write

recallCount.title: read-only: number of times the memory has been recalled; ignored on write

isSummary.title: read-only: true for the summary memory created by ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary; not updatable via UpdateMemory

group.title: optional freeform grouping/context label (system, subsystem, owner, ...); max 128 characters

placement.title: write-only: rank relative to existing values (see SignificancePlacement)

links.title: associative links this memory declares, weighted into its value (see consolidation.linkSignificanceWeight). Outbound only - Link is a directed edge from the item carrying it, so this lists exactly the edges this memory owns and an export/import round trip reproduces them once each; ask GetMemoryLinks for both directions. Write-only on StoreMemory (targets must already exist) and populated on read only when requested; use LinkMemories/UnlinkMemories to edit them incrementally

linkSignificance.title: read-only: sum of this memory's links' significance values, inbound and outbound, calculated by the server; ignored on write

metadata.title: optional multi-dimensional classification (source=slack, project=..., author=...), where group is the single freeform label. Keys match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,63}; values are any UTF-8 up to 512 bytes; at most 32 keys and 4096 bytes of serialised JSON in total, and those bytes count toward memory.limit.sizeBytes alongside the body. On UpdateMemory a non-empty map REPLACES the stored map wholesale - there is no per-key merge, and an absent or empty map leaves it untouched (use clear_metadata to remove it). Opaque to the server: filterable via GetMemories/SearchMemories, never interpreted, and never emitted as a metric, span, or log attribute

clearMetadata.title: write-only: on UpdateMemory, remove all metadata. Exists because the map's own emptiness cannot say it - an absent map and an explicitly empty one are the same on the wire, and every other updatable field reads unset as "leave unchanged". Ignored on StoreMemory; takes precedence over any metadata supplied alongside it

clearGroup.title: write-only: on UpdateMemory, reset group to empty, for the same reason clear_metadata exists - an empty group string otherwise means "leave unchanged". Ignored on StoreMemory; takes precedence over any group supplied alongside it

HippocampusUpdateMemoryBody.description:
Memory is a blob, opaque to the server, with a significance and timestamp, optionally linked to
an event. Recalling it (RecallMemories) reinforces it: the decay clock resets and its effective
significance rises. is_binary controls whether the body is indexed for content search (see
SearchMemories) - a binary body is never indexed.

SignificancePlacementMode.title:
- UNSPECIFIED: ignore placement; use the absolute significance value
 - ABOVE: rank just above the anchor, below the next-higher value
 - BELOW: rank just below the anchor, above the next-lower value
 - BETWEEN: rank strictly between the anchor (lower) and upper bounds

v1Bool.description:
Bool is a tri-state boolean (rather than proto3's inherent bool) so a caller can distinguish an
explicitly-set value from one left absent. It carries Memory.is_binary - where UNSPECIFIED and
FALSE are treated identically by the server (both mean not-binary) and only TRUE marks a memory
as binary - and the boolean list filters (GetMemoriesRequest's recalled/is_summary/is_binary),
where the distinction matters rather more: a proto3 bool cannot say "only the memories whose
is_summary is false", because an unset bool and an explicit false are the same byte on the wire.

 - UNSPECIFIED: not set; on Memory.is_binary the server treats this the same as FALSE, on a filter it applies no restriction
 - FALSE: explicitly false
 - TRUE: explicitly true

v1ClearRequest.description:
Clear deletes exactly the records captured by the Export/Transfer run that produced the
manifest: memories are deleted only if neither created nor recalled since the snapshot, and
events only once they have no memories left. Manifests are held in memory - a restart discards
them.

significance.title: the combined significance projected, echoed back

maxAgeDays.title: the span actually projected over, whether requested or chosen by the server

crossingAgeDays.title: the age at which the curve falls below deletion_threshold; -1 when it does not within the projected span

v1DecayCurve.description:
DecayCurve is the projected decay of one significance value under the current configuration,
sampled evenly from just after age zero to max_age_days. It is computed by the same code that
decides consolidation, so a plot of it cannot drift from what the service will actually do.

significance.title: the combined significance to project; must be > 0 - pass a memory's effective_significance to plot that memory's own curve

maxAgeDays.title: the span to project over; <= 0 asks the server to choose a span that shows the threshold crossing

points.title: samples to return; <= 0 selects the default (60), values above the cap (500) are clamped down to it

v1DecayCurveRequest.description:
DecayCurveRequest asks for the curve the configured decay algorithm produces for one significance
value, so a client can plot it without reimplementing the maths (which is what
docs/consolidation.md's value tables describe, and what the config wizard's preview approximates).
Leaving the field unset asks for no curve.

v1DecayPoint.description:
DecayPoint is one sample of a decay curve: the value the configured algorithm gives an item of the
requested significance once its decay clock reads age_days.

beforeTime.title: UnixNano; deletes records forgotten before this

all.title: delete every record; ignored when before_time is set

v1DeleteForgottenMemoriesRequest.description:
DeleteForgottenMemoriesRequest empties the forgotten log. Supply before_time to delete only what
was forgotten before it, or all to empty the log entirely - one of the two is required, so an
empty request can never silently discard the whole log.

id.title: auto-generated UUID if omitted on create; max 128 characters

timeStart.title: UnixNano; defaults to the current time when unset (0) on create; required (> 0) once defaulted

timeEnd.title: UnixNano; 0 means the event has not ended yet (see EndEvent); when set, must not be before time_start

significance.title: 0 = unranked (rank it later via UpdateEventSignificance/placement); must be >= 0; higher ranks more significant

memoriesConsolidated.title: read-only: true once a sleep cycle has deleted (consolidated) some of this event's memories; ignored on write

linkSignificance.title: read-only: sum of this event's links' significance values, inbound and outbound, calculated by the server; ignored on write

links.title: links this event declares to other events, weighted into its memories' value (see consolidation.linkSignificanceWeight). Outbound only, like Memory.links - ask GetEventLinks for both directions

memories.title: populated on read only when requested (GetEventById/GetEvents); write-only input on StoreEvent, stored via the same rules as StoreMemory

group.title: optional freeform grouping/context label (system, subsystem, owner, ...); max 128 characters

placement.title: write-only: rank relative to existing values (see SignificancePlacement)

metadata.title: optional multi-dimensional classification, exactly as Memory.metadata: same key charset, same 32-key/512-byte-value/4096-byte bounds, same replace-wholesale semantics on update, same opacity to the server

clearMetadata.title: write-only: on UpdateEvent, remove all metadata (see Memory.clear_metadata for why the empty map cannot say it)

clearGroup.title: write-only: on UpdateEvent, reset group to empty (see Memory.clear_group)

memoryCount.title: read-only: memories currently attached to this event, populated only when asked for (GetEventsRequest.memory_counts, GetEventByIdRequest.memory_counts - see there for why it is opt-in); 0 otherwise, which is indistinguishable from an event holding none, so ask for the count if you need to tell them apart. Counted within the caller's group scope, exactly as the nested memories are filtered. Ignored on write

v1Event.description:
Event is a named time span with its own significance, optionally carrying links to
other events and/or nested memories. memories/links are populated on read only when
requested (GetEventById, GetEvents); on StoreEvent nested memories are write-only input, each
stored via the same rules as StoreMemory.

memoryIds.title: the memories to value; at most 200 per call

curve.title: optional projected curve for the current configuration

v1ExplainConsolidationRequest.description:
ExplainConsolidationRequest asks where the named memories stand against the consolidation rules,
and optionally for the decay curve of the current configuration. Both parts are optional: ids
without a curve values just those memories, a curve without ids reports the configuration and the
current capacity pressure alone. Ids that do not exist are simply absent from the response.

capacityPressure.title: multiplier applied to the deletion threshold by how full the store is (1.0 = no effect)

deletionThreshold.title: the scaled threshold actually applied: deletionThreshold * capacity_pressure

capacityBytes.title: consolidation.capacityBytes; 0 when no byte capacity is configured

memoryCount.title: memories currently stored - the other axis capacity pressure rides on

capacityMemories.title: consolidation.capacityMemories; 0 when no row capacity is configured

method.description:
The configured decay policy, so a client can label what it is showing without a second source
of truth for it.

consolidation.method (1-6; see docs/consolidation.md)

unitsOfAgeInDays.title: days per unit of age fed to the decay algorithm

v1ExplainConsolidationResponse.description:
ExplainConsolidationResponse carries the decision inputs, one valuation per memory found, and the
requested curve. The inputs are a snapshot: capacity pressure and used bytes are re-read
periodically rather than per call, so they may lag a cycle that has just run - by design, since
this is asked far more often than a preview and both readings cost a scan.

v1ExportRequest.description:
Export snapshots every event and memory into an archive object in S3 and records a manifest of
exactly what was captured; with clear set, the captured records are deleted after a successful
upload (writes and recalls landing mid-run survive, exactly as Clear does).

eventId.title: empty for a memory with no event

significance.title: the memory's stored significance, as ranked

value.title: the computed decayed value that decided it (see docs/consolidation.md)

threshold.title: the capacity-pressure-scaled deletion threshold value was compared against

bodyBytes.title: stored size of the body, after compression - the same measure capacity accounting uses

timeRecalled.title: UnixNano of the most recent recall; 0 if never recalled

v1ForgetCandidate.description:
ForgetCandidate is one memory a cycle would delete, with the numbers behind the decision. value
and threshold are the two sides of the comparison that decided it: a CONSOLIDATION candidate is
one whose value fell below the threshold. Bodies are never included - a preview reports what
would be lost, it is not a way to read the store.

v1ForgetRule.description:
ForgetRule names why a memory appears in a consolidation preview - which of the two independent
deletion paths selected it. The distinction matters when tuning: a memory forgotten by
CONSOLIDATION decayed below the threshold and is answered by the decay settings
(aggressiveness, deletionThreshold, unitsOfAgeInDays), while one forgotten by EVICTION was
still valuable enough to keep and went only because the store is over its byte capacity - which
is answered by capacityBytes, or by storing less.

 - FORGET_RULE_CONSOLIDATION: decayed value fell below the capacity-pressure-scaled deletion threshold
 - FORGET_RULE_EVICTION: still above the threshold, but evicted to bring the store back under its byte capacity

seq.title: the log's own monotonic key; pass the lowest seen back as after_seq to page

eventId.title: empty for a memory with no event

significance.title: the memory's significance, as ranked when it went

value.title: its computed decayed value at that moment (see docs/consolidation.md)

threshold.title: the capacity-pressure-scaled deletion threshold then in force

bodyBytes.title: stored size of the body it held, after compression

timeRecalled.title: UnixNano of its last recall; 0 if never recalled

v1ForgottenMemory.description:
ForgottenMemory is one record from the forgotten log: a memory the sleep cycle deleted, and the
decision that took it. value and threshold are the two sides of the comparison as they stood at
that moment - the threshold moves with capacity pressure, so recording it is what keeps value
interpretable afterwards.

There is no body, and there never will be: this says a memory was forgotten, not what it said.

totalCount.title: events matching the filter, ignoring limit/offset — for pagination

nextSeq.title: pass as after_seq for the next page; 0 when the page is the last

v1GetForgottenMemoriesResponse.description:
GetForgottenMemoriesResponse carries one page of the log. total counts every record the log
holds within the caller's scope, not the filtered subset, so a client can show how much history
exists behind the page it is looking at.

enabled reports whether the service is currently recording. It matters because an empty page is
ambiguous without it: nothing has been forgotten, or nothing is being written down.

linkSignificance.title: the queried item's total link significance, both directions - the figure the decay maths damps and weights

totalCount.title: memories matching the filter, ignoring limit/offset — for pagination

scanEnabled.description:
scan_enabled reports whether this instance runs the candidate scan at all: it needs
consolidation.summarisationMinMemories > 0 AND consolidation.enabled, since the scan is part of
the sleep cycle and a replica runs none. It exists because an empty candidates list is
ambiguous in the way that matters, exactly as WhoAmI.groups is - "nothing is due yet" and "this
instance will never offer you anything" are opposite answers, and only one of them is worth
waiting on. A client presenting an empty list must branch on this rather than on the list.

v1ImportBatchRequest.description:
ImportBatchRequest carries full-state rows (original timestamps, recall state, significance,
group, event links) to be upserted by id into the store as-is - a data migration, not a fresh
write. It is the ingest half of Transfer and is re-sendable: re-importing the same rows is
idempotent.

id.title: the linked memory's or event's id; must name an existing item of the same kind

significance.title: this link's weight; 0..1000000, must not be negative - not part of the significance registry, never ranked

v1Link.description:
Link is a directed, significance-carrying association between two memories or between two events.
One Link message describes one edge from the item carrying it to the item it names.

The significance is weighted into the decay maths for BOTH ends, with diminishing returns - the
contribution is consolidation.linkSignificanceWeight * log1p(sum of an item's link significances),
so a well-connected memory decays more slowly without any number of links ever making it
unforgettable. Unlike the event relationships this replaces, both ends must exist: a link is
deleted automatically when either end is forgotten, so it can never dangle.

v1LinkDirection.description:
LinkDirection narrows which of an item's links a read returns. The graph is stored directed, so
the two directions are distinguishable, but value is symmetric - both ends of a link gain its
significance - which is why BOTH is the default rather than OUTBOUND.

 - LINK_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: treated as BOTH
 - LINK_DIRECTION_BOTH: links in either direction
 - LINK_DIRECTION_OUTBOUND: only links this item declared, pointing away from it
 - LINK_DIRECTION_INBOUND: only links other items declared, pointing at it

id.title: the far end's id - the other memory or event

direction.title: OUTBOUND when the queried item declared this link, INBOUND when the far end did

created.title: UnixNano the link was first created

v1LinkEdge.description:
LinkEdge is one stored link as read back: the pair it connects, its significance, and which way
it points relative to the item that was asked about. Link (the write form) names only the far
end, because the near end is the item carrying it; a read can return both directions at once and
so has to say which is which.

id.title: auto-generated UUID if omitted on create; max 128 characters

timeStamp.title: UnixNano; defaults to the current time when unset (0) on create; required (> 0) once defaulted

significance.title: 0 = unranked (rank it later via UpdateMemory/placement); must be >= 0; higher ranks more significant. On UpdateMemory, 0 with no placement leaves the existing significance unchanged - it cannot reset a memory to unranked

eventId.title: optional: leave unset to store the memory unassociated with any event

body.title: required (non-empty) on create; a proto3 string, so always valid UTF-8 on the wire - encode true binary payloads (e.g. base64) before setting is_binary; optionally capped by memory.limit.sizeBytes (0 = unlimited)

isBinary.title: set once at creation; not updatable via UpdateMemory. TRUE bodies are opaque and never indexed for content search (see SearchMemories)

timeRecalled.title: read-only: UnixNano of the most recent recall (RecallMemories, or SearchMemories with reinforce); 0 if never recalled; ignored on write

recallCount.title: read-only: number of times the memory has been recalled; ignored on write

isSummary.title: read-only: true for the summary memory created by ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary; not updatable via UpdateMemory

group.title: optional freeform grouping/context label (system, subsystem, owner, ...); max 128 characters

placement.title: write-only: rank relative to existing values (see SignificancePlacement)

links.title: associative links this memory declares, weighted into its value (see consolidation.linkSignificanceWeight). Outbound only - Link is a directed edge from the item carrying it, so this lists exactly the edges this memory owns and an export/import round trip reproduces them once each; ask GetMemoryLinks for both directions. Write-only on StoreMemory (targets must already exist) and populated on read only when requested; use LinkMemories/UnlinkMemories to edit them incrementally

linkSignificance.title: read-only: sum of this memory's links' significance values, inbound and outbound, calculated by the server; ignored on write

metadata.title: optional multi-dimensional classification (source=slack, project=..., author=...), where group is the single freeform label. Keys match [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,63}; values are any UTF-8 up to 512 bytes; at most 32 keys and 4096 bytes of serialised JSON in total, and those bytes count toward memory.limit.sizeBytes alongside the body. On UpdateMemory a non-empty map REPLACES the stored map wholesale - there is no per-key merge, and an absent or empty map leaves it untouched (use clear_metadata to remove it). Opaque to the server: filterable via GetMemories/SearchMemories, never interpreted, and never emitted as a metric, span, or log attribute

clearMetadata.title: write-only: on UpdateMemory, remove all metadata. Exists because the map's own emptiness cannot say it - an absent map and an explicitly empty one are the same on the wire, and every other updatable field reads unset as "leave unchanged". Ignored on StoreMemory; takes precedence over any metadata supplied alongside it

clearGroup.title: write-only: on UpdateMemory, reset group to empty, for the same reason clear_metadata exists - an empty group string otherwise means "leave unchanged". Ignored on StoreMemory; takes precedence over any group supplied alongside it

v1Memory.description:
Memory is a blob, opaque to the server, with a significance and timestamp, optionally linked to
an event. Recalling it (RecallMemories) reinforces it: the decay clock resets and its effective
significance rises. is_binary controls whether the body is indexed for content search (see
SearchMemories) - a binary body is never indexed.

eventId.title: empty for a memory with no event (or one whose event no longer exists)

significance.title: the memory's own stored significance, as ranked

effectiveSignificance.title: what the decay actually acts on: the memory's own significance plus its event's, the damped link contributions below, and the weighted recall count

threshold.title: the capacity-pressure-scaled deletion threshold value is compared against

ageDays.title: days since the memory's decay clock last reset - its creation, or its most recent recall

timeRecalled.title: UnixNano of the most recent recall; 0 if never recalled

wouldConsolidate.title: a cycle running now would forget this memory

retained.title: held by consolidation.minimumRetentionInDays, so neither consolidation nor capacity eviction may take it

belowMinimumAge.title: younger than consolidation.minimumAgeInDays, so value-based consolidation is deferred whatever the value says

daysUntilForgotten.title: projected days until the memory would be consolidated, holding today's threshold and pressure and assuming no further recall; 0 when it is already due, -1 when it is not due within the projected horizon

linkSignificance.title: the memory's own summed link significance, both directions, before damping

linkContribution.title: what those links add to effective_significance: linkSignificanceWeight * log1p(link_significance)

eventLinkSignificance.title: the memory's event's summed link significance, both directions, before damping; 0 for a memory with no event

eventLinkContribution.title: what the event's links add to effective_significance, damped the same way; 0 for a memory with no event

v1MemoryValuation.description:
MemoryValuation is where one memory stands against the consolidation rules right now: the value
the decay algorithm gives it, the threshold that value is measured against, and the flags that
override the comparison either way. Bodies are never included - this explains a memory, it is not
a way to read one.

mergeTo.title: the surviving event; must already exist

mergeFrom.title: the event whose memories are moved to merge_to; need not exist - an absent one simply matches no memories

memoriesConsolidated.title: memories whose value fell below the threshold

memoriesEvicted.title: memories capacity eviction would additionally delete

eventsDeleted.title: events that would go: those left with no memories, plus empty events past their own threshold

bytesFreed.title: estimated bytes reclaimed by both paths together, on the same basis as used_bytes

memoriesRetained.description:
memories_retained counts the memories that would otherwise have been forgotten but are held
by consolidation.minimumRetentionInDays, with retained_bytes their stored size. Watch this
against capacity_bytes: retention overrides the capacity target, so once retained_bytes
approaches capacity_bytes the store cannot be brought back under its target however hard
eviction runs. They are counted, never listed - on a healthy store almost everything is
retained, so listing them would return the store.

capacityPressure.description:
The decision inputs as they stood for this preview, so the numbers above can be read against
the configuration that produced them.

multiplier applied to the deletion threshold by how full the store is (1.0 = no effect)

deletionThreshold.title: the scaled threshold actually applied: deletionThreshold * capacity_pressure

capacityBytes.title: consolidation.capacityBytes; 0 when no byte capacity is configured, in which case eviction never runs

truncated.title: true when more memories would be forgotten than limit returned

v1PreviewConsolidationResponse.description:
PreviewConsolidationResponse reports what a cycle would forget. The counts and byte figures are
always complete; candidates is a bounded sample of the individual memories, ordered by value
ascending so the least valuable - those furthest past the threshold - come first.

The preview accounts for the cycle's own ordering: consolidation runs first, so the memories it
would delete are excluded from the eviction pool and their bytes are already reclaimed before
eviction is considered at all. A memory therefore appears at most once, under the rule that
would actually claim it.

includeLinked.title: also return the memories linked to those recalled, one hop, in either direction. The linked memories are returned as an associative recall, not counted as directly recalled: their recall_count is untouched (see consolidation.linkRecallPropagation for what a recall does to a neighbour's decay clock)

limit.title: maximum results; a value <= 0 selects the default (10)

eventId.title: optional: restrict matches to a single event

reinforce.title: route matches through recall, reinforcing them

group.title: optional: restrict matches to memories carrying this group label

mode.title: how to match; unset means KEYWORD

includeLinked.title: also return the memories linked to each match, one hop, in either direction; appended after the ranked matches and never counted as matches themselves

metadata.title: optional: restrict matches to memories whose metadata carries every one of these "key=value" pairs (AND, exact match), exactly as GetMemoriesRequest.metadata. Applied inside the search index rather than to the results, so it narrows the candidates that ranking sees and limit still means what it says

v1SearchMemoriesRequest.description:
SearchMemoriesRequest queries the secondary content-search index for memories matching the
query. Results are always re-read from the primary store, which remains authoritative; ids the
index returns that the primary store no longer holds are silently dropped. When reinforce is
true the matched memories are recalled - resetting their decay clocks and raising their
effective significance - rather than merely fetched, and only the memories actually returned are
reinforced.

v1SearchMode.description:
SearchMode selects how a search decides which memories match.

Not every mode is available in every deployment, and which are is a property of the deployment
rather than of the caller: KEYWORD needs a content-search backend (built in on the sqlite driver,
OpenSearch otherwise), while SEMANTIC and HYBRID additionally need an embedding model and
OpenSearch's vector index. An unavailable mode is rejected with FAILED_PRECONDITION naming what
is missing; WhoAmI reports the available modes so a client can choose without probing.

 - SEARCH_MODE_UNSPECIFIED: treated as KEYWORD, so an existing caller's behaviour is unchanged
 - SEARCH_MODE_KEYWORD: match on the words in the body; exact terms, error codes, and identifiers
 - SEARCH_MODE_SEMANTIC: match on meaning via embeddings; finds paraphrase the words would miss
 - SEARCH_MODE_HYBRID: both, their rankings fused; usually the best of the three

v1SignificanceExtremum.description:
SignificanceExtremum selects "all events tied at the highest (or lowest) significance value"
instead of a min/max range - the tied set is computed dynamically from whichever events match
GetEventsRequest's other filters (time range, group), not a fixed value the caller supplies.
Mutually exclusive with significance_min/significance_max (InvalidArgument if both are set).

 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_UNSPECIFIED: no extremum filtering; significance_min/significance_max (if set) apply as a normal range
 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_HIGHEST: return only events at the highest significance value among those matching the other filters
 - SIGNIFICANCE_EXTREMUM_LOWEST: return only events at the lowest significance value among those matching the other filters

anchor.title: anchor significance value; must be >= 1 unless anchor_id is set

anchorId.title: anchor by an existing item's id, whose significance is looked up; that item must already be ranked (significance > 0)

upper.title: BETWEEN only: the upper bound significance; must be >= 1 (and greater than anchor) unless upper_id is set

upperId.title: BETWEEN only: the upper bound by an existing item's id; that item must already be ranked (significance > 0)

v1SignificancePlacement.description:
SignificancePlacement positions an item's significance relative to existing values instead of
taking the absolute `significance` field. It exists because significance is a dense integer with
no room between adjacent values: this lets a client say "just above the 5s" or "between 5 and 6"
and have the server open a gap for it. Write-only on StoreEvent/StoreMemory/UpdateMemory and
UpdateEventSignificance; it is never populated on read responses. When mode is UNSPECIFIED the
absolute `significance` value is used as-is (0 meaning unranked).

v1SortDirection.description:
SortDirection reverses the order a listing's order_by field sorts in (GetEventsRequest.order_dir,
GetMemoriesRequest.order_dir).

UNSPECIFIED keeps each order_by value's NATURAL direction rather than meaning "ascending": the
magnitude and time fields sort descending (most significant, most recent, most recalled first -
which is what a listing is nearly always asked for, and what every one of these listings did
before there was a direction to set), while the lexical ones - id, group, and an event's name -
sort ascending, alphabetical order being the only reading of those anyone wants first. The
natural direction of each value is stated on order_by itself.

 - SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED: sort in the order_by field's natural direction (see above)
 - SORT_DIRECTION_ASC: ascending, whatever the field's natural direction
 - SORT_DIRECTION_DESC: descending, whatever the field's natural direction

id.title: the stored event's id; empty when the event was not retained

memoryCount.title: nested memories retained (best-effort; those rejected/dropped are not reported individually)

rejected.title: true when the event was dropped for significance below event.minimumSignificance

v1StoreEventResponse.description:
StoreEventResponse carries the stored event's id and how many of its nested memories were
retained. An event whose significance is below event.minimumSignificance is quietly forgotten,
like a brain that simply does not retain the insignificant: no error is returned, id is empty,
memory_count is 0 (its nested memories are not stored either), and rejected is true.

Nested-memory creation is best-effort: the event is committed first, so a nested memory that
fails validation, is dropped for insignificance, or hits a store error does not fail the event
create and is not individually reported here - memory_count is only the count actually retained.
Store memories individually if you need per-memory success/failure.

id.title: the stored memory's id; empty when the memory was not retained

rejected.title: true when the memory was dropped for significance below memory.minimumSignificance

v1StoreMemoryResponse.description:
StoreMemoryResponse carries the stored memory's id. A memory whose significance is below
memory.minimumSignificance is quietly forgotten, like a brain that simply does not retain the
insignificant: no error is returned, id is empty, and rejected is true.

v1SummarisationCandidate.description:
SummarisationCandidate identifies an event whose memories have accumulated enough, and gone
quiet for long enough, to be worth condensing into a single summary memory via
ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary.

memoriesReplaced.title: how many memories the summary replaced

summary.title: the LLM-generated summary text stored in the new memory

v1TransferRequest.description:
Transfer streams every event and memory directly to a centralised instance's ImportBatch RPC
(address from transfer.targetAddress); like Export it records a manifest, and with clear set
deletes the captured records once the target has accepted them all.

searchModes.description:
search_modes lists the SearchMemories modes this deployment can serve, so a client can adapt
rather than discover an unavailable mode by having a search rejected. It depends on the
storage driver and on whether OpenSearch and an embedding model are configured - never on the
caller - so it is the same for every caller of a given instance. An empty list means content
search is unavailable entirely and SearchMemories is rejected in every mode.

groups.description:
groups is the caller's group scope: the group labels whose records this token may read and
write. Empty means unscoped - the whole store - which is what every token is unless the
deployment issues scoped ones, so a client must read group_scoped rather than infer from the
list being empty.

groupScoped.description:
group_scoped reports whether a scope is in force for this caller. It exists because an empty
groups list is ambiguous on its own and the two readings are opposites: unscoped (see
everything) versus scoped to nothing. A client showing "you can see N groups" must branch on
this, not on len(groups).

When true, writes are stamped with the caller's group, Purge/Sleep/PreviewConsolidation are
refused, and records outside the scope report NotFound - so a console can explain an empty
store rather than leave it looking like data loss.

summariserEnabled.description:
summariser_enabled reports whether this deployment has the embedded LLM configured
(ollama.enabled), i.e. whether SummariseMemories can serve. Reported for the same reason as
search_modes and with the same properties: it is a property of the deployment rather than the
caller, so a client can offer service-authored summarisation only where it exists instead of
discovering its absence through a FAILED_PRECONDITION. It says nothing about
ReplaceMemoriesWithSummary, which needs no summariser - the caller writes that summary.

v1WhoAmIResponse.description:
WhoAmIResponse reports the caller's identity to a client so it can tailor its UI. role is the
caller's effective authorization tier ("reader", "writer", or "admin"); auth_enabled is false
when the service runs without authentication, in which case role is "admin" (unrestricted) and
client_id is empty.
